name: The Luce household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: luce_william

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 July 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-07-02, 1 day later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-07-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1835-05-20 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

persons.name: William Luce

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: GRADED BY THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER — rule G2e, applied 2026-09-04. This identity is inferred because that rung fired on the civic and press rows recorded on this card, which the resident-research corpus does not read. This programme's letter-list rule of 2026-09-02 would call it a projected resident on the absence of a research row; it is superseded here, and a no-find in one corpus is not a finding about another (T-0822). KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, AND HELD THERE MORE THAN ONCE. The papers print 'Luce, William' and 'William Luce 2' in 2 separate returns of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 2 July 1834, column 29; the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13 — across 1834-07-02 to 1835-05-20. A name in a LATER return is somebody still being written to, months on, which is the strongest thing a letter list can say about residence and is why this person outranks a single-return name of the same surname. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.summary: Racine County old-settlers history says William Luce was already in Captain Knapp's cabin at Racine when a party came from Chicago on January 2, 1835. The rare exact name and regional chronology are strong, but this evidence points away from Chicago residence at the May 1835 postal date.

candidates.basis: Exact name in January 1835 southeastern Wisconsin pioneer account.
conflicts: Documented at Racine before the May 1835 Chicago letter list.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
